modules.title: Introduction to Cattle Nutrition and Feedstuffs
lessons: Overview of beef cattle industry and feeding systems
Digestive anatomy and physiology of ruminants
Nutrient requirements: energy, protein, minerals, vitamins
Common feed ingredients: grains, forages, protein meals
Feed quality and safety considerations
Regulatory and labeling requirements for feed

modules.title: Nutrient Requirements and Feeding Standards
lessons: Using NRC and BR-CORTE tables for nutrient requirements
Determining dry matter intake in cattle
Energy systems: TDN, ME, NE for maintenance and gain
Protein systems: CP, DIP, UIP, metabolizable protein
Mineral and vitamin supplementation guidelines
Adjusting requirements for environmental factors

modules.title: Feed Ingredient Evaluation and Analysis
lessons: Proximate analysis: moisture, ash, protein, fat, fiber
In vitro and in situ digestibility techniques
Near-infrared reflectance spectroscopy (NIRS) for feed evaluation
Energy estimation from chemical composition
Anti-nutritional factors and mycotoxin screening
Interpreting feed analysis reports

modules.title: Formulation Basics and Mathematical Methods
lessons: Pearson square and algebraic methods for two-ingredient mixes
Simultaneous equations for multi-ingredient formulations
Linear programming concepts for least-cost formulation
Using spreadsheet software for feed formulation
Setting nutrient constraints and ingredient limits
Evaluating and adjusting formulated diets

modules.title: Energy and Protein Sources in Cattle Diets
lessons: Cereal grains and by-products: corn, barley, wheat, DDGS
Oilseed meals: soybean, cottonseed, canola meals
Roughage sources: hay, silage, crop residues
Urea and non-protein nitrogen utilization
Rumen degradable and undegradable protein sources
Balancing energy-to-protein ratios

modules.title: Mineral and Vitamin Nutrition
lessons: Macro minerals: calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, potassium
Micro minerals: zinc, copper, manganese, selenium
Vitamin requirements: A, D, E, and K
Bioavailability of mineral sources
Mineral interactions and antagonists
Formulating mineral supplements and premixes

modules.title: Feed Additives and Supplements
lessons: Ionophores and their effects on feed efficiency
Probiotics, prebiotics, and direct-fed microbials
Buffers and neutralizers for high-grain diets
Enzymes and feed processing aids
Growth promotants and implants: regulations and use
Flavors, binders, and pelleting aids

modules.title: Formulating Diets for Different Production Stages
lessons: Starter diets for newly received calves
Growing and finishing diets for steers and heifers
Diets for breeding bulls and cows
Transition and adaptation diets
Creep feeding and backgrounding diets
Diet formulation for drought or emergency feeding

modules.title: Feed Processing and Manufacturing
lessons: Grinding, rolling, and cracking grains
Pelleting and extrusion processes
Mixing and batching procedures
Silage making and preservation
Total mixed ration (TMR) preparation
Quality control in feed manufacturing

modules.title: Least-Cost Formulation and Software Applications
lessons: Principles of least-cost diet formulation
Using linear programming software (e.g., Brill, Feedsoft)
Setting up ingredient databases and nutrient profiles
Sensitivity analysis and shadow prices
Formulating with alternative ingredients
Evaluating economic returns of formulated diets

modules.title: Feedlot Management and Feeding Strategies
lessons: Feedlot layout and bunk management
Step-up and step-down feeding programs
Monitoring feed intake and performance
Managing acidosis and bloat
Feed delivery and weighing accuracy
Record keeping and data analysis for feedlot efficiency

modules.title: Case Studies and Practical Formulation Exercises
lessons: Case study: Formulating a finishing diet for steers
Case study: Developing a supplement for grazing cattle
Case study: Least-cost formulation with by-products
Case study: Troubleshooting a feedlot diet
Practical exercise: Using software to formulate a diet
Final project: Complete diet formulation and justification
